distribution.title: Uniform distribution
distribution.intro: A continuous uniform random variable on \([a,b]\), with \(a<b\), assigns equal density to equal-length intervals within its support.
distribution.formula: Its density is \(f(x)=1/(b-a)\) for \(a\le x\le b\), and zero otherwise. Inside that interval, \(F(x)=(x-a)/(b-a)\).
distribution.properties: The mean is \((a+b)/2\) and the variance is \((b-a)^2/12\). For \(U\sim U(0,1)\), suitable inverse CDFs transform \(U\) into samples from other distributions.
distribution.course: The course uses uniform random variables in the inversion method and a uniform model on [0, θ] in a worked UMVUE example.
distribution.course_link: Estimate the upper endpoint of a uniform distribution
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
